newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Tired All Blacks get grim news.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Tired All Blacks get grim news.

text.p: WELLINGTON, July 14 - Mentally tired All Blacks who have taken longer than expected to freshen heard news on Monday that South Africa's two outstanding forwards are fit for Saturday's Tri-series rugby opener.
Lock Mark Andrews and flanker Ruben Kruger will definitely play in the Johannesburg test after they satisfied Springbok coach Carel du Plessis they were fit, NZPA reports.
But fiery hooker James Dalton is expected to miss the match due to a calf muscle injury.
Northern Transvaal prop Marius Hurter and Gauteng No 8 Warren Brosnihan were also added to the Bok squad.

Andrews is expected to replace Gauteng's Hannes Strydom and Kruger will play the open-side flank in place of Free State's Johan Erasmus. The other tip from the Springbok camp is that Natal's Henry Honiball may replace Jannie de Beer at first-five.
Honiball's strong defence could be favoured because of Springbok worries about the running game of either Carlos Spencer or Andrew Mehrtens at first-five. Honiball would also do the goalkicking.
The All Blacks arrived in Pretoria early today (NZ time) after several days' rest and recreation at Pilansberg Game Park near Sun City. But coach John Hart is wondering whether it has been enough.
"The value of coming here early has really been shown, because the guys have shown they are a lot more tired after four tests than we realised," said Hart.
"All they wanted to do was sleep. They were pretty lethargic."
Two or three players have yet to sort out normal sleep patterns.
"But it was very peaceful on the game farm," said Hart.
Tomorrow the players touch a ball for the first time on the trip.
Hart promises the most physical session of the week to wake them up, "but judging by the fitness test we had yesterday at the game farm, we have nothing to worry about in that way".

The All Black team will be named tomorrow night (NZ time), with the only real question mark being over the first five-eighth position, where Mehrtens' fine test goalkicking record could sway things in his favour.
The only other questions are whether Alama Ieremia, whom the South Africans fear greatly, may take a midfield place and whether Glen Osborne's greater experience may be preferred to Tana Umaga.
